correctness.rationale: The flat semantic clause is correctly reduced to I_w(A)⊆B for upsets. Arbitrary valuations A,B,C force di iff I_w preserves binary unions; choosing C=I_w(A)∪I_w(B) establishes necessity. The key nonstandard step is checked: finiteness expresses every upset as a finite union of principal upsets, so preservation is equivalent to (PC), with witnesses expanded in both directions. Empty successor rows and nonantisymmetric preorders are included. The O(n^5) bound uses an O(n^3) subset preprocessing table and O(n^3) trigger triples with O(n²) candidates. Independent standalone exhaustive semantics and condition checks agree for all 14914 labelled frames of orders at most three. The all-size proof is symbolic, not inferred from enumeration.

value.rationale: The natural open structural question left by the 2026 source is exactly which finite flat frames validate di. The theorem replaces a one-way, overly restrictive directedness test by a polynomial-time necessary-and-sufficient first-order correspondence, covering arbitrary preorders and arbitrary R. The smallest possible non-directed valid frame shows the distinction is genuine and semantically interpretable: future accessible witness rows can jointly recover a branching row even though that row itself has no common lower bound. This is structural and motivated rather than a bare finite table or routine parameter variation.
